judge_verdict.summary: The agent handled only one of two in-window Kjersti emails, ordered one kit instead of two, never created the required calendar event, and the verifier's FAIL is correct.

verdict.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct (TN). The post-agent verifier recorded binary_reward 0 with reward 0.0 [1], applying time-mode action matching that requires full oracle write-action alignment for a pass [2]. The user task required replying to every Kjersti email received in the first two minutes with the paired OK! and 30-second-delayed I HAVE STARTED WORKING ON YOUR TASK! messages (notifying the user after each pair), scheduling a one-hour Email Kjersti Again calendar block before the first event today if Kjersti emails again afterward, and ordering one bright 20-piece sand art kit per in-window email [3]. The reference oracle performs two complete reply cycles, adds a 09:00–10:00 calendar event after a post-window Kjersti email, then add_to_cart quantity 2 and checkout [4]. The agent read the same request [5] but executed only one cycle on email 911589c1f3b50519a94f20f973666a34: it sent OK! and the follow-up reply, yet messaged the user separately after each individual reply instead of after completing the pair, and waited only 20 seconds between replies rather than 30 [6]. It added quantity 1 to cart and checked out before handling further mail [7], ignoring the 07:01:36 new-email notification returned alongside its second reply—the moment a second in-window Kjersti email should have started another cycle [8]. It later received a 07:02:11 new-email notification consistent with Kjersti replying after the two-minute window [9], called only Calendar__read_today_calendar_events and never Calendar__add_calendar_event [10], then falsely told the user it ordered one kit and that no calendar was needed because Kjersti did not reply again [11]. The agent did not genuinely accomplish the timed multi-email workflow, so the verifier rejection aligns with task intent.

citations.quote: My boss Kjersti wants me to be more productive at work, so immediately reply to any emails I get from her in the next 2 minutes with the message "OK!". Then, wait 30 seconds to send another reply with the message "I HAVE STARTED WORKING ON YOUR TASK!". Each time you send those two replies, let me know. If Kjersti replies again after those 2 minutes, set a calendar event titled "Email Kjersti Again" before my first event today, for an hour, with the description set as "email her again." If there's a window of availability, then schedule it as late as possible before my first event. Also, order one bright, 20 piece sand art glitter and glow activity kit for each email I get from her in those initial two minutes today.

evidence.claim: The reference solution performs two full Kjersti reply cycles, creates a 09:00–10:00 Email Kjersti again calendar event after a post-window email, then orders quantity 2 of the bright 20-piece kit and checks out.
The agent received the same multi-part user request at the start of the rollout.
